kitDescription: Jill is a slow-firing magnum-style AR attacker (2.5 shots/sec, 9-round magazine) whose damage comes from normal attacks plus an acid DoT. Her passive raises her normal-attack multiplier by 30% for each 9-round magazine and makes the first round after every reload-to-max apply a sustained acid burn of 192% of final ATK per second for 30 seconds — with her ~2s magazine cycle this burn is effectively always on. She gains +40.03% ATK for 10 seconds whenever any team Full Burst begins, and +34.99% True Damage for 10 seconds whenever she casts her own burst. Her burst dumps her entire magazine to force an immediate reload (re-arming both passives), fixes her reload speed for 10 seconds, and grants +80.78% Hit Rate, +75% Attack Damage, and converts her normal attacks to true damage for 10 seconds. In the sim the reload-speed lock and the true-damage conversion are documented as unmodeled (no engine primitive / measurement gate), which leaves the +34.99% True Damage line currently inert.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA. The S5 run is RED on 8 assertions, but every red classifies cleanly: four (#1/#2/#3/#8) are the permanent-passive-vs-durationShots encoding choice on Magnum Ammo, which the blind S6 override's own caveat concedes is numerically identical at jill's 9-round magazine (and the driver's byte-identical-dot scoping proof is strictly stronger than the blind ratio test that failed on a 1.5% differencing artifact — #3 is a RECON_ERROR on tolerance); #4 is the blind S5 test contradicting the blind S6 override on trueDamagePct inertness (both driver and S6 leave trueNormals unmodeled for the same schema-gap reason); #5 is a false blind inertness premise (acid damage feeds burst gauge — removing it drops team FBs 12→11, so the comp coupling is a system effect, not a scope leak); #6/#7 are the owner-ruled reload clamp, where the blind S6 itself concedes the schema cannot express a clamp. The blind override and the driver converge on every contested disposition (both unmodeled lines, the maintained-DoT reading, both trigger identities), and the driver's 18-assertion spec discriminates against each named nearest-wrong model (generic Damage-Up for J1, burstCast for J4, consumeAmmo removal for J7). Two same-model residuals for the owner to spot-check: (1) the reload-clamp owner ruling — if 'fixed at a 99.96% increase' is ever re-read as the literal boost, the sim currently charges ~1.4s of forced-reload downtime per cast the kit would not pay, making this the highest-leverage open read on the unit; (2) the trueNormals measurement gate — the Takina primitive exists, so holding the conversion (and the entire 34.99% trueDamage line) inert on a 'do not re-fudge' gate is a judgment call the owner may want to convert into an enact-and-regrade increment; (3) the acid maintained-vs-stacking reading is a shared design-arithmetic hypothesis across all agents, never measured — stable, but a single popup-cadence read would settle it. None of these block GO: every divergence is documented with estimate, recipe, and tier, and the two unmodeled lines are corroborated by the independent blind derivation.
